# wordsworth

**Generate Morse practice text the Wordsworth way — words, not characters**

- **Version recorded:** 0.3
- **Categories:** `cw`, `training`
- **Upstream:** <https://sourceforge.net/projects/kb1oiq-k1ig-wordsworth/>

## What it does

Two small Perl tools implementing K1IG's "Wordsworth" method of Morse training: gen_cw_words emits random words from built-in lists (common CW words, letters, names, numbers) for head-copy practice, and text_to_cw converts any text file into practice material. Pipe either into a CW audio tool such as ebook2cw.

## Why you would want it

The Wordsworth method (QST, 2019) trains hearing whole words instead of counting dits -- the widely recommended path past the 10 WPM plateau. These are the author-adjacent reference tools, co-published by AHRL's own maintainer.

## Before it will work

A CW audio generator to feed -- ebook2cw or the ebook2cwgui this catalog carries. Perl is already on every Debian-family system.

## How it installs

- prebuilt tarball from https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/kb1oiq-k1ig-wordsworth/wordsworth/wordsworth_0.3.tar.gz
  - The SourceForge artifact hashes identically to the copy AHRL bundles -- verified 2026-08-30, both downloads. Perl itself is essential on every target; no dependency line needed.

Binaries this produces:

- `gen_cw_words.pl` → `gen_cw_words`
- `text_to_cw.pl` → `text_to_cw`

## Known problems

None known. The upstream tarball also carries QSO_Words_5000.txt, sample QSO text worth feeding to text_to_cw -- grab it from the archive if you want it; nothing installs it system-wide.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- Effectively finished software; 0.3 has stood since 2021.

The SourceForge project (KB1OIQ and K1IG).
